items.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
items.summary: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

items.title: Fifa staff asked to attend interviews as Infantino sell-off scheme investigated
items.summary: Democrats to examine Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal Infantino could be subpoenaed to give evidence A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal. Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration. Continue reading...

items.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
items.summary: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil. Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United, whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...
